items.title: Norris wins wet São Paulo race as Mercedes seals Constructors’ title
items.summary: FIA Document 81 confirms Norris won the 71-lap wet-dry-wet race in 1:35:23.504, 14.602 seconds ahead of Verstappen; Hadjar completed the podium. The final classification matches Formula1.com. FIA Document 82 records Mercedes on 652 points after Brazil; Formula1.com reports that the team clinched the 2026 Constructors’ title.
items.why_it_matters: Norris converted pole, Verstappen climbed from P21, and Mercedes secured the teams' championship. The result is now final rather than provisional.

items.title: Leclerc and Hamilton call São Paulo a disaster after Ferrari’s lowest-scoring weekend since Monza
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Leclerc and Hamilton described Ferrari’s pace and tyre performance in stark terms. Leclerc finished eighth after a post-race five-second penalty, while Hamilton finished ninth; the report calls it Ferrari’s lowest-scoring weekend since Monza.
items.why_it_matters: The drivers’ comments document frustration with this weekend’s performance; they do not establish a new team-order policy or a technical cause.

items.title: Final FIA classification applies three five-second penalties
items.summary: FIA Documents 78, 79 and 80 impose five seconds on Oliver Bearman for an unsafe release, Charles Leclerc for contact with Liam Lawson, and Kimi Antonelli for an unsafe release. Formula1.com also reports Leclerc's post-race penalty. Document 81's final order places Lawson seventh, Leclerc eighth, Antonelli fifth and Bearman 17th; its current result table agrees. Document 76 lists lap-time deletions separately, while Document 77 reports the inspected cars complied.
items.why_it_matters: The penalties changed the final order and points; deleted laps and the earlier summons are separate from the three timed sanctions.

items.title: Hamilton reaches 400 starts and scores in São Paulo
items.summary: Formula1.com identifies the São Paulo Grand Prix as Hamilton’s 400th F1 start. The final classification places him ninth, one lap down, with two points after starting 20th.
items.why_it_matters: A career milestone also ended in a points finish; the final result confirms his ninth place.

items.title: Verstappen describes his P21-to-podium drive as a challenging race
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Verstappen started P21, reached second after a strong opening intermediate stint and finished 14.602 seconds behind Norris. He said the car later had a "weird balance"; Hadjar completed a Red Bull double podium in third.
items.why_it_matters: The comeback and changing conditions shaped the podium battle, but Verstappen's account of the balance issue is his description, not a confirmed technical diagnosis.
